items.followUp: Draw and label a mitochondrion, and explain how its structure supports cellular respiration.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the main parts and showing the inner membrane folds and matrix in the diagram.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for correctly describing the double membrane and cristae, and 1 mark for a suitable labelled diagram including the matrix.

rubric.why: The main function of mitochondria is to release usable energy as ATP during cellular respiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that mitochondria are the site of cellular respiration and produce ATP.

rubric.why: Mitochondria contain their own DNA and ribosomes in the matrix.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning mitochondrial DNA and ribosomes in the matrix.

modelAnswer: Mitochondria are double-membraned organelles found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells.
The smooth outer membrane encloses an inner membrane; the inner membrane folds inward to form cristae.
The space enclosed by the inner membrane is the matrix, which contains enzymes, circular DNA and ribosomes.

Mitochondria are the sites of cellular respiration, where energy is released from food and stored in ATP.

items.followUp: Name the five kingdoms and give one characteristic of each kingdom.

rubric.why: Monera includes organisms with prokaryotic cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Monera and correctly stating that its organisms are prokaryotic.

rubric.why: Protista consists mainly of simple, mostly unicellular eukaryotes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Protista and stating that its organisms are eukaryotic, mostly unicellular.

rubric.why: Fungi are eukaryotic heterotrophs that obtain nutrients by absorption.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Fungi and giving a correct characteristic such as heterotrophic nutrition by absorption.

rubric.why: Plants are multicellular eukaryotes that generally make their own food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Plantae and stating that its organisms are generally multicellular autotrophs.

rubric.why: Animals are multicellular eukaryotes and their cells lack cell walls.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Animalia and giving a correct characteristic such as multicellularity or absence of cell walls.

modelAnswer: The five-kingdom system proposed by R. H. Whittaker classifies organisms using features such as cell type, body organisation and mode of nutrition.
Monera: prokaryotic, usually unicellular organisms, such as bacteria.
Protista: eukaryotic organisms, mostly unicellular, such as Amoeba.
Fungi: eukaryotic heterotrophs that absorb nutrients; their cell walls generally contain chitin.
Plantae: multicellular eukaryotes that usually make food by photosynthesis and have cellulose cell walls.
Animalia: multicellular eukaryotes that obtain food by ingestion and have no cell walls.

items.followUp: Describe the roles of ATP and NADPH produced during the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Light absorbed by chlorophyll supplies energy for the light reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chlorophyll absorbs light energy.

rubric.why: Water is split, releasing oxygen, hydrogen ions and electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing photolysis of water and identifying oxygen as a product.

rubric.why: Electron transport provides energy for ATP formation by photophosphorylation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that ATP is formed using energy from electron transfer.

rubric.why: NADP accepts hydrogen/electrons and is reduced to NADPH.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that NADP is reduced to NADPH.

modelAnswer: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy and its electrons become excited.
Water molecules split by photolysis into hydrogen ions, electrons and oxygen; oxygen is released.
Excited electrons pass along electron carriers, and their energy is used to make ATP by photophosphorylation.
NADP accepts electrons and hydrogen ions and is reduced to NADPH.

items.followUp: Explain anaemia and haemophilia, and state how each affects the blood.

rubric.why: Anaemia involves too few red blood cells or insufficient haemoglobin, reducing oxygen transport.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing anaemia as a deficiency of red blood cells or haemoglobin and linking it to reduced oxygen-carrying capacity.

rubric.why: Haemophilia is an inherited disorder in which blood does not clot normally.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying haemophilia as an inherited clotting disorder that causes prolonged bleeding.

rubric.why: Leukaemia is a cancer involving abnormal production of white blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing leukaemia as cancer or abnormal uncontrolled production of white blood cells.

rubric.why: Thalassaemia is an inherited disorder affecting haemoglobin production and can cause anaemia.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking thalassaemia to defective haemoglobin production and resulting anaemia.

modelAnswer: Anaemia: a condition in which the blood has too few red blood cells or too little haemoglobin, reducing its oxygen-carrying capacity.
Haemophilia: an inherited disorder in which blood fails to clot normally, so bleeding may continue for a long time.
Leukaemia: a cancer of blood-forming tissues that causes abnormal, uncontrolled production of white blood cells and interferes with normal blood-cell production.
Thalassaemia: an inherited disorder in which haemoglobin is made abnormally; it can cause fragile red blood cells and anaemia.

items.followUp: Define physiology and state how it differs from anatomy.

rubric.why: Anatomy is the study of the structure of organisms, particularly their internal parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying anatomy as the study of structure and 1 mark for specifying the internal structure or parts of organisms.

modelAnswer: Anatomy is the branch of biology that studies the internal structure of organisms.

items.followUp: State two important contributions of Ibn al-Haytham to scientific study.

rubric.why: Jabir Bin Hayan is credited in the textbook with introducing experimental research in science.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that he introduced or promoted experimental methods in science.

rubric.why: His work included books on plants and animals, and he is widely known as a founder or father of chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning his writings on plants and animals or identifying him as the father/founder of chemistry.

modelAnswer: Jabir Bin Hayan introduced experimental methods in scientific research.
He wrote books on plants and animals and is known as the father of chemistry.

items.followUp: Name the six major bio-elements that make up most of the mass of living organisms.

rubric.why: Bio-elements are the chemical elements that occur in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining bio-elements as elements present in living organisms.

rubric.why: The textbook identifies about 16 elements as occurring in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that about 16 bio-elements occur in living organisms.

modelAnswer: Bio-elements are the chemical elements present in living organisms.
About 16 elements occur in living organisms; six of them—carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus and sulphur—make up about 99% of body mass.

items.followUp: Give one example of a qualitative observation and one example of a quantitative observation.

rubric.why: A qualitative observation describes a quality or characteristic without giving a measurement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable descriptive observation, such as stating that leaves are green.

rubric.why: A quantitative observation gives a numerical measurement or count.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable observation containing a numerical measurement, such as a plant being 10 cm tall.

modelAnswer: Qualitative observation: The leaves are green.
Quantitative observation: The plant is 10 cm tall.
